record.provider: Telegram — MTProto user account + unlimited channels as the volume

free_tier.stated: No total storage cap, quoted from Telegram: 'you can ... share an unlimited number of photos, videos and files (doc, zip, mp3, etc.) of up to 2 GB each'. Per-file 2 GB free, 4 GB with Premium. Per-account volume is effectively unbounded because you can hold up to 500 channels/supergroups (1000 with Premium) and create up to 50 channels per day, and each channel is a separate unbounded blob store.

egress.terms: Free and unmetered. Telegram charges nothing for downloads and imposes no transfer quota; the only egress cost is Telegram's own speed shaping. Downloads are free even for files uploaded by Premium users: 'any user can download large 2+ GB files uploaded by premium users'.

record.tooling: Strongest tooling of any provider in this whole research area. MTProto clients: TDLib (github.com/tdlib/td, 9.2k stars, pushed 2026-10-21), MadelineProto (github.com/danog/MadelineProto, 3.5k stars, pushed 2026-10-21, alive). Field-proven storage layer: Teldrive (github.com/tgdrive/teldrive, 3.1k stars) with its own rclone backend (github.com/tgdrive/rclone). CAUTION: Telethon (12.1k) and Pyrogram (4.6k) are both ARCHIVED (Telethon read-only since 2026-02-21, Pyrogram since 2024-12-23). Do not start a new build on either.
record.chaining: Unbounded by construction: 1 account x 500 channels x unlimited posts = unlimited. A second account carries a second read allowance, not a second storage allowance. Teldrive adds its own layer: 'channel-part-limit: 500000' parts per channel with 'auto-channel-create: true'. It opens a NEW channel automatically when the active one fills, so the sharding is already automated. A 2 GB file is 4000 x 512KB parts, so one channel holds ~250 TB of max-size files before rotation.

record.limits_note: Per-file 2 GB free / 4 GB Premium. Verified against Telegram's own config, not a blog: upload_max_fileparts_default = 4000 and upload_max_fileparts_premium = 8000, times the max part size 524288 bytes = 2,097,152,000 B and 4,194,304,000 B. Upload speed is throttled for non-Premium by an explicit server error, FLOOD_PREMIUM_WAIT_X, which signals 'upload speed is limited because the current account does not have a Premium subscription'; upload_premium_speedup_upload = 10, i.e. Premium is ~10x faster. No published daily byte cap exists — Telegram documents none, and the empirical field report (Teldrive issue #561) is 10-50 GB/day for one user, with a maintainer answering 'I have seen user posting that they upload 400-500gb daily no issues. It depends on how many bots you have.' Treat 20 GB/day as folklore: no primary source found.
record.reliability_note: Throttling is the real risk, not deletion: FLOOD_PREMIUM_WAIT_X caps non-Premium throughput and FLOOD_WAIT_X backs off per method. Files persist indefinitely in practice, but a closed account takes its channels with it, and Teldrive's own README warns accounts and stored files 'can become unavailable', so a store that spans several accounts loses only the parts one account holds.

per_object_cap.stated: 4 GB per file, against 2 GB on a free account.
per_object_cap.notes: no byte-exact boundary is published; the FAQ says '4 GB'

retention.stated: Cloud chat media is kept until deleted. Telegram's FAQ: 'you can keep all your media in the cloud without deleting things'.
retention.notes: no retention window is stated for cloud chats; secret chats are excluded from the cloud entirely

egress.terms: 'Subscribing lifts any media download speed limits from your account on Telegram's side.' Non-subscribers can still fetch a Premium user's 2 GB+ file: 'any user can download large 2+ GB files uploaded by premium users.'
egress.free_allowance: no byte allowance; the throttle is speed, not volume

record.interface_detail: Purchased and managed through the user or @PremiumBot; the upload ceiling applies to the account, not to an API.
record.tooling: Any MTProto client or TDLib-based tool inherits the account's tier; Bot API bots do not, because a bot has no Premium tier of its own.
record.chaining: Turns 2 GB objects into 4 GB objects for a TDLib or MTProto client, halving the object count of 1 TiB of monthly transfer; it does not lift any bot's 20 MB/50 MB limit.

limits.value: media download speed limits are lifted only for subscribers

record.binding_note: 1 TiB/month at 4 GB is 256 objects; the object ceiling is still the first wall, and flood control is unreachable at that count.

identity_cost.detail: A paid subscription. The FAQ says the first payment's currency and price follow 'the country code of the phone number of your Telegram account', so the price is country-specific and was not read as a number.

record.reliability_note: A free account downloading large media is speed-limited on Telegram's side; a Premium lapse returns the account to 2 GB objects and the speed limit immediately.
record.confidence_note: Features and the speed sentence are on the Premium FAQ read. The price is deliberately not stated because the page states no figure.

record.notes: The price is a live gap: the FAQ defers it to the phone number's country, and @PremiumBot is the only quoter. Abandon the record if the 4 GB figure moves; re-check t.me/premium/5 at the same time.
